desc: Prove descending-value greedy: each inverted pair crosses once, largest-first minimizes each crossing's index (frozen larger values already at the right).
Derive per-value formula: c_k = #{v < k | pos[v] < pos[k]}, p_k = c_k + 1, cost_k = sum_{j=p_k}^{k-1} j = (p_k + k - 1)(k - p_k)/2.
Implement the O(N log N) Fenwick solution in Python (read N, P from stdin; print answer to stdout) using the per-value formula.
Validate on provided samples (expect 4, 6, 0) and against an exhaustive brute force over all permutations with N ≤ 7.
Sanity-check worst case N = 2*10^5 (reversed permutation) for runtime and that Python big-int accumulation is correct.
